01 / The constraint

The constraint

Build the hardware of a small computer from basic logic gates, then translate Hack assembly into 16-bit machine code.

02 / The implementation

What I built

Logic gates written in a hardware description language (HDL), an arithmetic logic unit (ALU), memory, a program counter and memory-mapped input/output. The Python assembler separates parsing, code generation, symbol handling and orchestration.

03 / A deliberate choice

The tradeoff

Explicit translation tables keep instruction encoding readable. A first pass records label addresses; a second resolves symbols and emits instructions. I used Python so I could write and inspect the translation rather than copy the tutorial implementation.

04 / Evidence, with its limits

What the work showed

Built through the hardware portion, reached 16K memory, implemented an ALU capable of 18 operations via 6 control bits, and generated .hack binaries from .asm programs.
